The son of [[Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame|Hall of Fame]] basketball coach [[Jim Boeheim]], he played [[college basketball]] for the [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse Orange]]. ==High school career== Boeheim attended [[Jamesville-DeWitt High School]] in [[DeWitt, New York]].{{cite news|first=Gaurav|last=Shetty|title=The best stories from Buddy Boeheim's high school and Syracuse career |url=https://dailyorange.com/2022/03/best-stories-buddy-boeheims-high-school-syracuse-career/|work=[[The Daily Orange]]|date=March 23, 2022|access-date=March 27, 2022}} As a junior, he averaged 26.3 points and 9.8 rebounds per game, leading his team to a Class A [[Section 3 (NYSPHSAA)|Section III]] title, and was named All-Central New York Large School Player of the Year.{{cite web|first=Mike|last=Waters|title=Syracuse basketball commit Buddy Boeheim is more than walk-on son of a coach|url=https://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/2017/09/syracuse_commit_buddy_boeheim_is_more_than_the_walk-on_son_of_a_coach.html|work=[[The Post-Standard]]|date=September 8, 2017|access-date=March 20, 2021}} For his senior season, Boeheim transferred to [[Brewster Academy]] in [[Wolfeboro, New Hampshire]], where he served as team captain.{{cite web|first=Mike|last=Waters|title=Syracuse basketball commit Buddy Boeheim named captain at Brewster Academy|url=https://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/2017/11/syracuse_basketball_commit_buddy_boeheim_named_captain_at_brewster_academy.html|work=[[The Post-Standard]]|date=November 3, 2017|access-date=March 20, 2021}} He committed to playing college basketball at [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse]], where his father was serving as head coach, over offers from [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]] and [[UMass Minutemen basketball|UMass]].{{cite web|first=Charlie|last=DiSturco|title=3-star Buddy Boeheim officially commits to Syracuse|url=http://dailyorange.com/2017/09/3-star-buddy-boeheim-officially-commits-to-syracuse/|work=[[The Daily Orange]]|date=September 8, 2017|access-date=March 20, 2021}} ==College career== Boeheim came off the bench in his freshman season at Syracuse, averaging 6.8 points per game.{{cite web|first=Matthew|last=Gutierrez|title=After 1st year with his dad, Buddy Boeheim got no special treatment|url=http://dailyorange.com/2019/03/1st-year-dad-buddy-boeheim-got-no-special-treatment/|work=[[The Daily Orange]]|date=March 22, 2019|access-date=March 20, 2021}} He entered the starting lineup as a sophomore and averaged 15.3 points.{{cite news|first=Adam|last=Zagoria|title=The Son Shoots, the Father Shouts, and Syracuse Keeps Winning|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2021/03/25/sports/ncaabasketball/buddy-boeheim.html|work=[[The New York Times]]|date=March 25, 2021|access-date=March 25, 2021}}{{cite web|first=Nick|last=Andre|title=Syracuse Basketball: Buddy Boeheim must emerge in 2020–21 season|url=https://bustingbrackets.com/2020/11/24/syracuse-basketball-buddy-boeheim-must-emerge-2020-21-season/|website=BustingBrackets.com|date=November 24, 2020|access-date=March 20, 2021}} On March 11, 2021, Boeheim scored a career-high 31 points in a 72–69 loss to [[2020–21 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|Virginia]] at the [[2021 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]] quarterfinals.{{cite web|first=Mike|last=Waters|title=Buddy Boeheim scores career-high 31 points, makes father proud in Syracuse loss|url=https://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/2021/03/buddy-boeheim-scores-career-high-31-points-in-syracuses-loss-to-virginia.html|work=[[The Post-Standard]]|date=March 11, 2021|access-date=March 20, 2021}} In his next game, on March 19, he scored 30 points in a 78–62 first-round win over sixth-seeded [[2020–21 San Diego State Aztecs men's basketball team|San Diego State]] at the [[2021 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]].{{cite magazine|first=Talha|last=Rao|title=Syracuse Dominates San Diego State to Advance in NCAA Tournament|url=https://www.si.com/college/syracuse/basketball/syracuse-dominates-sdsu-ncaa-tournament|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=March 20, 2021|access-date=March 20, 2021}} As a junior, Boeheim averaged 17.8 points and 2.6 assists per game, while shooting 38.3 percent from [[Three-point field goal|three-point]] range.{{cite news|first=Matthew|last=Gutierrez|title=Ten thoughts on Syracuse's 10 scholarship players as the Orange reload after a Sweet 16 run|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/2579132/2021/05/11/ten-thoughts-on-syracuses-10-scholarship-players-as-the-orange-reload-after-a-sweet-16-run/|work=[[The Athletic]]|date=May 11, 2021|access-date=October 5, 2021}} He was named to the [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball teams|All-ACC]] First Team as a senior.{{cite press release|title=ACC Unveils 2021–22 Men's Basketball Awards|url=https://theacc.com/news/2022/3/6/athlete-awards-acc-unveils-2021-22-mens-basketball-awards.aspx|website=TheACC.com|publisher=[[Atlantic Coast Conference]]|date=March 7, 2022|accessdate=March 7, 2022}} ==Professional career== ===Detroit Pistons / Motor City Cruise (2022–2024)=== After going undrafted in the [[2022 NBA draft]], Boeheim signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Detroit Pistons]].{{cite web|title=Pistons sign Buddy Boeheim to two-way contract|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/34184813|website=ESPN.com|date=July 2, 2022|access-date=July 14, 2022}} Boeheim later joined the Pistons' [[2022 NBA Summer League]] team.{{cite web|title=Detroit Pistons 2022 NBA2K23 Summer League Roster|url=https://www.nba.com/summer-league/2022/vegas/team/1610612765/pistons|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 14, 2022}} In his Summer League debut, Boeheim scored no points, going 0-for-2 from the field in around nine minutes in an 81–78 win against the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].{{cite web|title=Portland Trail Blazers vs Detroit Pistons Box Score|url=https://www.nba.com/game/por-vs-det-1522200002/box-score#box-score|website=NBA.com|date=July 8, 2022|access-date=July 14, 2022}} Four nights later he scored a team-high 18 points for the Pistons in a loss to the [[Indiana Pacers]].{{cite web|title=Indiana Pacers vs Detroit Pistons Box Score|url=https://www.nba.com/game/det-vs-ind-1522200036/box-score|website=NBA.com|date=July 12, 2022|access-date=October 20, 2022}} In July 2023, Boeheim joined the Pistons for the [[2023 NBA Summer League]]{{cite web|title=DETROIT PISTONS 2023 NBA 2K24 SUMMER LEAGUE ROSTER|url=https://www.nba.com/summer-league/2023/vegas/team/1610612765/pistons|website=NBA.com|access-date=October 8, 2023}} and on October 2, he signed a standard contract with them.{{cite tweet|author=Pistons PR|title=The @DetroitPistons announced today the team's 2023–24 training camp roster including the signing of Buddy Boeheim, Tosan Evbuomwan, Jontay Porter, Zavier Simpson and Stanley Umude to Exhibit 10 contracts.|number=1708851868766462316|user=Pistons_PR|date=October 2, 2023|access-date=October 8, 2023}} However, he was waived on October 21{{cite tweet|author=Pistons PR|title=The Detroit Pistons announced today that the team has requested waivers on Buddy Boeheim, Tosan Evbuomwan, Jontay Porter and Zavier Simpson.|number=1715844213722534289|user=Pistons_PR|date=October 21, 2023|access-date=October 30, 2023}} and nine days later, he joined the [[Motor City Cruise]].{{cite tweet|author=Motor City Cruise|title=The engine is revving, and we're ready to roll! Check out the Motor City Cruise training camp roster – we're ready to work! HustleAndDrive|number=1719088094782132699|user=MotorCityCruise|date=October 30, 2023|access-date=November 8, 2023}} On February 23, 2024, Boeheim signed a standard contract with Detroit.{{cite tweet|author=Pistons PR|title=The @DetroitPistons announced today that the team has signed Stanley Umude to a contract and signed guard Buddy Boeheim and forward Tosan Evbuomwan to two-way contracts.|number=1761074632289890744|user=Pistons_PR|date=February 23, 2024|access-date=February 23, 2024}} However, he was waived on June 29.{{cite web|first=Alex|last=Kirschenbaum|title=Pistons Waive Troy Brown Jr., Buddy Boeheim|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/06/pistons-to-waive-troy-brown-jr.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=June 29, 2024|access-date=June 29, 2024}} ===Oklahoma City Blue (2024–2026)=== On October 16, 2024, Boeheim signed with the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]],{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Thunder Sign Buddy Boeheim, Cut Alex Reese|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/10/thunder-sign-buddy-boeheim-cut-alex-reese.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=October 16, 2024|access-date=October 18, 2024}} but was waived two days later.{{cite web|first=Rory|last=Maher|title=Hornets’ Charlie Brown Jr. Among Latest NBA Cuts|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/10/hornets-charlie-brown-jr-among-latest-nba-cuts.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=October 18, 2024|access-date=October 19, 2024}} On October 25, he joined the [[Oklahoma City Blue]].{{cite web|title=2024-2025 Oklahoma City Blue Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Oklahoma-City-Blue/38/Transaction_History/2025|website=RealGM.com|access-date=November 11, 2024}} Boeheim signed with the Thunder on October 14, 2025.{{cite news |last1=Sen |first1=Saugat |title=Former Syracuse guard Buddy Boeheim lands with new NBA team |url=https://www.si.com/college/syracuse/basketball/syracuse-buddy-boeheim-okc-thunder-01k7k2ne3xzq |access-date=December 20, 2025 |work=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=October 16, 2025}} He was waived the following day in order to join the Blue.{{cite web |last1=Anderson |first1=Erik |title=Thunder Waive Son of Legendary Coach |url=https://heavy.com/sports/nba/oklahoma-city-thunder/thunder-waive-son-of-legendary-coach/ |website=Heavy.com |access-date=December 20, 2025 |date=October 15, 2025}} On February 7, 2026, Boeheim agreed to a two-way contract with the Thunder. This followed the waiving of [[Chris Youngblood (basketball)|Chris Youngblood]].{{Cite web |date=2026-02-06 |title=Thunder's Buddy Boeheim: Agrees to two-way deal with OKC |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/thunders-buddy-boeheim-agrees-to-two-way-deal-with-okc/ |access-date=2026-02-07 |website=CBS Sports |language=en}} He made four appearances for Oklahoma City, averaging 1.5 points. On March 2, the Thunder waived Boeheim.{{Cite web |last=Martinez |first=Justin |date=March 2, 2026 |title=OKC Thunder waives Buddy Boeheim, signs Payton Sandfort to two-way contract |url=https://www.oklahoman.com/story/sports/nba/thunder/2026/03/02/okc-thunder-waives-buddy-boeheim-signs-payton-sandfort-two-way-contract/88943817007/ |access-date=2026-03-02 |website=The Oklahoman |language=en-US}}{{Cite web |date=March 2, 2026 |title=Thunder sign Payton Sandfort to two-way deal, waive Boeheim |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/48082672/thunder-sign-payton-sandfort-two-way-contract-waive-buddy-boeheim |access-date=March 7, 2026 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press |language=en}}
